readerTitle: Not every partnership needs a wedding
caseNote: 가상 사례 2개 (부티크 호텔 + 동네 베이커리, 반려견 미용 예약 앱 + 결제 회사) · 파트너십 유형 구분은 일반적인 경영 개념
insight: 파트너십의 종류는 '서로 무엇을 얼마나 깊이 묶는가'의 사다리이며, 목표를 이루는 가장 느슨한 단계부터 고르고 근거가 생길 때 한 칸씩 올라간다.
misconception: 파트너십은 깊을수록(공동 투자, 합작 회사) 진지하고 좋은 것이다. 혹은 반대로, 느슨한 제휴면 무엇이든 충분하다.

sources.text: 파트너십 유형(소개·공급/유통·통합·합작/지분) 구분은 경영 전략의 일반 개념을 단순화한 것
호텔·베이커리, 예약 앱·결제 회사 사례와 모든 조건은 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 사례는 모두 가상이며 실제 수치나 기업 사실을 쓰지 않았습니다. 유형 이름(referral, supply, integration, joint venture)은 업계마다 부르는 말이 다를 수 있으니 용어 표기를 편집 단계에서 한 번 더 확인하세요.
수익 배분(SAL-07-04), 독점(SAL-07-05), 종료(SAL-07-06)와 겹치지 않도록 해당 내용은 언급만 하고 설명하지 않았습니다. 형제 레슨 확정 후 중복 여부를 다시 점검하세요.

cards.title: Not every partnership needs a wedding
body: A small hotel says it has partnered with the bakery down the street. A scheduling app says it has partnered with a payments company.
Same word. But one deal might be a stack of paper vouchers, and the other might be shared code and shared customers. Knowing *which kind* you need saves months of the wrong commitment.

image.label: A hotel and a bakery linked by a thin string, a phone and a card reader linked by a thick cable
image.brief: 화면을 반으로 나눈 일러스트. 왼쪽: 작은 호텔과 빵집이 가는 실 한 가닥으로 연결. 오른쪽: 스마트폰과 카드 단말기가 굵은 케이블로 연결. 따뜻한 플랫 스타일, 실제 로고나 상표 없음.

cards.title: Your hotel has no kitchen. Guests keep asking about breakfast.
body: You run a 20-room hotel. A well-loved bakery café is two minutes away. You're not sure how many guests would actually pay for breakfast.
What kind of deal do you start with?

options.text: Co-invest with the bakery to open a café in your lobby
options.feedback: You'd get a real breakfast offer, but you'd share rent, staff and ownership before knowing guests will pay. Hard to undo if demand is weak.

options.text: Give guests a breakfast voucher for the bakery, and settle up monthly
options.feedback: Cheap to start and easy to stop, and it tells you how many guests want breakfast. You give up control over the experience in return.

options.text: Have the bakery deliver pastries every morning for you to serve
options.feedback: Guests get breakfast on site, but you take on daily orders, waste and serving before you know the demand.

cards.title: Four kinds of partnership, from loose to tight.
body: Each step up, the two businesses share more, and walking away gets harder.

breakdown.label: Referral
breakdown.detail: You send customers to each other. You share leads.

breakdown.label: Supply or resale
breakdown.detail: One sells or uses the other's product. You share a product.

breakdown.label: Integration
breakdown.detail: Your products or processes connect. You share how work gets done.

breakdown.label: Joint venture
breakdown.detail: You build something new together. You share ownership and risk.

cards.title: Partnership types are levels of commitment
body: The **type of partnership** is defined by what each side puts in and how hard it is to leave. A referral costs little and ends with a phone call. A joint venture can take lawyers to end.

Deeper isn't better or worse. Each level buys you something: more control, more effort from the partner, a better customer experience. And each costs something: money, time, and freedom to change course.

image.label: A four-step ladder labeled referral, supply, integration, joint venture
image.brief: 네 칸 사다리 인포그래픽. 아래부터 "Referral", "Supply", "Integration", "Joint venture". 오른쪽에 위로 갈수록 두꺼워지는 화살표 두 개: "What you share", "Cost to leave".

cards.title: Same ladder, different starting rungs.
body: The hotel didn't know if guests wanted breakfast. So the lowest rung made sense: vouchers test demand for almost nothing. If most guests use them, a daily pastry supply deal becomes worth the hassle.

A scheduling app for dog groomers is in a different spot. Groomers already take payment at every appointment, and they keep asking to do it inside the app. Demand is proven. A referral link would send them away mid-task. Here, the job calls for a higher rung from day one.

image.label: Hotel on the bottom rung, app on the third rung
image.brief: 같은 사다리 두 개를 나란히. 왼쪽 사다리 맨 아래 칸에 작은 호텔 아이콘, 오른쪽 사다리 세 번째 칸에 휴대폰 속 강아지 아이콘. 실제 앱 로고 없음.

cards.title: Pick the loosest type that does the job.
body: Start by naming the job: test demand, reach new customers, improve the product, or build something neither of you could alone.
Then choose the lowest rung that gets that job done. Climb only when you have evidence, such as repeat use or customer requests. Each rung you climb should be a decision you've earned, not a default.

cards.title: Loose deals get loose effort.
body: A referral partner has little reason to push your product. If the bakery is busy, your voucher guests may wait. Low commitment often means low priority.

Going too deep has the opposite cost. Shared ownership can trap both sides after the market changes. Whatever the level, how each side is rewarded matters as much as the type itself. That's the next lesson.

cards.title: Now it's the dog-grooming app.
body: Your groomers want to take card payments inside your app. A payments company offers several ways to work together. Which fits the job?

options.text: Add a link that sends groomers to the payment company's own site
options.feedback: Fast and free, but groomers leave your app mid-appointment. It solves a demand test you've already passed.

options.text: Connect payments into your app using the company's standard tools and terms
options.feedback: Groomers get paid without leaving your app, and you can still switch providers later. You take on build work and some dependence on their system.

options.text: Form a joint company with the payment firm to build a pet-business suite
options.feedback: Big upside if it works, but you'd share ownership and control for a problem a simpler connection already solves.

cards.title: Choose the partnership by the job, not by the word.
body: Referral, supply, integration, joint venture. Start at the loosest level that does the job, and climb only when the evidence says so.
**Try it today:** list your current or planned partners. Write which rung each one sits on, and whether that matches the job you need it to do.
